clue.text: Carriage with dicky seat-around noon, hop in

indicators.note: around says the shuffled seat letters go round the next pieces
dicky means shaky or unsound, so the letters of seat are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A coach with a wobbly seat, and someone hopping aboard at midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dicky' shuffles the seat letters to STAE, then 'around' splits them round the noon and hop pieces. A dicky seat is also a real folding rear seat on old carriages, which is the trap.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanhope is a light open horse-drawn vehicle, named after the clergyman who first had one built.

clue.text: Simpleton with a straw in his mouth?

definitions.meaning: a gullible person easily taken in

definitions.text: with a straw in his mouth?
definitions.meaning: someone drawing a drink up through a straw is one who sucks

explanation.definitionFit: A gullible dupe is called a sucker, and literally one who sucks through a straw is too.

clue.text: The tone of voice which may be grave

definitions.meaning: a manner of pronunciation, as of a region
a grave is one kind of mark written over a letter, alongside acute and circumflex

explanation.definitionFit: A way of pronouncing is an inflection of speech, and a grave is one type of written diacritic mark.

clue.text: Mounts tool on the end it's supposed to be lucky

indicators.note: on the end says the tool is placed after the mounts

parts.note: mounts are steeds you ride
a hoe is a garden tool

explanation.surface: Riding animals with an implement fixed on, said to bring good fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-shaped iron from a hoof is a traditional good-luck charm, hung over doors.

clue.text: Local patriotism dominating position

definitions.meaning: taken literally, pride in one's own town or district
the most prominent or honoured spot

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means the foremost spot of honour, and read word by word it means civic pride in a locality.

clue.text: Soul personified of spy converted by revolutionary

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so the letters of spy are rearranged

parts.note: Che Guevara is the crossword's stock revolutionary

explanation.surface: A secret agent's spirit is won over by a rebel.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the girl loved by Cupid was the embodiment of the human spirit.

clue.text: Good man in charge, he's had nothing to eat yet is quite impassive

indicators.note: to eat says the good man and in charge take the next piece inside them

parts.note: ST, saint, is the crossword's good man
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A virtuous leader who has eaten nothing stays perfectly calm.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who bears hardship without showing feeling is called a philosopher of the Stoa's school.

clue.text: Joined in and searched around

indicators.note: around says searched goes outside the word in

parts.note: combed means searched thoroughly
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone joined in the hunt and looked all around.
explanation.definitionFit: Things merged or united together are joined.

clue.text: In this state, folk are confined to one district

definitions.text: In this state, folk are confined to one district

parts.words: In this state, folk are confined to one district
parts.note: sounds like a local lockdown, but describes the biological condition of a species found only in one region

explanation.definitionFit: Biologists use the term for a species being native and restricted to a particular area.

clue.text: Squash, for example, in copper to restrain it

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
to curb is to restrain
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drink kept in a copper pot to hold it back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squash' looks like a drink or a game; here it is the vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Squashes, marrows and gourds belong to the gourd family of plants, cucurbits.

clue.text: Made one get into shallow water

indicators.note: get into says one goes inside the shallow water

parts.note: a ford is a shallow river crossing
one, said of oneself, gives ME

explanation.surface: Someone forced a person to wade into the shallows.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shaped or constructed has been formed.

clue.text: Wrapping up of the hands in net was silly

indicators.note: silly means foolish or muddled, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: hands are workers, men

explanation.surface: Wrapping the workers in a net was a foolish idea.
explanation.definitionFit: To swathe is to bind in cloth, and the noun names the act of such binding.

clue.text: The lad's pole stuck in lake

indicators.note: stuck in says the pole is pushed inside the lake

parts.note: Erie is one of North America's Great Lakes
N is the north pole

explanation.surface: A boy's punting pole has got stuck in a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy's name, so it serves for the lad.

clue.text: Much in use abroad where castration is the practice

indicators.note: abroad means scattered widely, so the letters of much in use are dispersed

explanation.surface: A habit commonly found in foreign lands involving gelding.
explanation.definitionFit: Being or making a gelded man is the practice the definition describes.

clue.text: Relays of shirt-makers?

parts.note: relays are teams taking turns, while a shift is also an old word for a shirt or chemise, so its makers are its workers

explanation.definitionFit: Employees who take turns covering round-the-clock hours are organised in relays.

clue.text: Tie the boat up, finish the game on board and start searching for fellow lodgers

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to moor is to tie up a boat
mate, checkmate, ends a game of chess

indicators.note: start means the opening letter of searching

explanation.surface: Sailors tie up, play out the chess game on deck, and go hunting for shipmates.
explanation.definitionFit: People sharing a lodging or bedroom are flatmates.

clue.text: Weapon bringing about armistice out East

indicators.note: about means around and changed, so the letters are rearranged
out says the east letter is dropped

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A sword ends up bringing a truce in the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes E from ARMISTICE to leave ARMISTIC, then 'about' shuffles it.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved oriental sword is a weapon.

clue.text: Sulky girl brought to book

parts.note: Petula is a girl's name
NT, the New Testament, is a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: A moody girl is brought to justice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought to book' looks like being held to account, but it just joins the girl to the book.
explanation.definitionFit: Peevish and bad-tempered is what a sulky person is.

clue.text: Making a girl prisoner inside the battlements

indicators.note: prisoner inside says the girl is held within making

parts.note: creation is the act of making
Nell is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl is being held captive within the castle walls.
explanation.definitionFit: Battlements are the notched parapet of a castle, the crenels and merlons.

clue.text: Copper does turn out to be valid currency

indicators.note: turn out means rearrange, so the letters are reshuffled

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A copper coin proves to be legal tender.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the Portuguese monetary unit, legal tender when the clue was set.

clue.text: Notice present and stick by it

parts.note: an ad is a notice
present means here, in attendance

explanation.surface: Put up a poster and keep your word to it.
explanation.definitionFit: To cling or be fixed to something is a synonym.

clue.text: Is bound to hurt, catching ring in man's hair

indicators.note: catching says the ring is caught inside

parts.note: must means is bound to
O is a ring shape
ache means hurt

explanation.surface: Getting a ring caught in a man's hair is sure to sting.
explanation.definitionFit: Facial hair grown on the upper lip, chiefly by men.

clue.text: Time to go on the wagon too, we hear

indicators.note: to go on places the time before the wagon

parts.note: a wain is a farm wagon

explanation.surface: Time to give up drinking as well, so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the wagon' means teetotal, which is the trap. The definition is said aloud: the word means two, which sounds like too.
explanation.definitionFit: The old word for two sounds the same as too.

clue.text: Doctor about to employ thought

indicators.note: about says the doctor goes round employ

parts.note: MD is a doctor of medicine
to use is to employ

explanation.surface: A physician is about to put an idea to work.
explanation.definitionFit: Pondered or reflected, the past tense of think.

clue.text: Leaves container, arriving at new gate without a key

indicators.note: without means outside, so the reworked gate goes round the next pieces
new says the letters of gate are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
B is a musical key

explanation.surface: Leaving with a box, someone reaches a new gate but has no key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' makes TEAG of GATE, and 'without' (outside) puts it round A and B. The leaves are tea leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A small porous sachet holds tea leaves for brewing.

clue.text: Taking things easy when others smoke

definitions.meaning: a medical treatment of bed and relaxation
read as the remainder being cured, as meat or tobacco is cured by smoking

explanation.definitionFit: A medical regime of enforced relaxation; curing is also preserving by smoke.

clue.text: Upbraiding a chap without braid

definitions.meaning: an ordinary naval seaman, with no officer's gold braid

explanation.definitionFit: A scolding is one sense; a non-commissioned sailor is the other, in the Royal Navy.

clue.text: Soot damaged clothing and doctor's equipment

indicators.note: damaged means broken up, so the letters of soot are rearranged

parts.note: a cope is a long ceremonial cloak worn by clergy

explanation.surface: Grime has spoilt the garments and the physician's kit.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrument for examining the ear, used by physicians.
